text:
maya: Heads up — seeing a sudden spike in 5xx (502/504 and some 500s) across the hosted API starting ~12:10 UTC. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% -> 6% in ~4m. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/xyz :rotating_light:
ashish: digging into gateway logs now. Most common message is 'upstream reset' and a bunch of `503` from auth-service. I can paste logs: 
```
12:11:03 gateway | upstream reset while sending to auth-service (id=auth-12)
12:11:04 gateway | 502 from upstream route-handler (id=route-7)
12:11:07 api    | request timeout after 10s (id=trace-ff7a)
```

kevin: Support is getting noisier — two enterprise customers opened severity-2 tickets complaining about timeouts and token failures. Sample trace ids: trace-ff7a, trace-ff93. Customers report 5xx body: `{"error":"gateway timeout"}`
emmie: I pushed routing config `route_v2_by_size` earlier for the rollout. I started a gradual rollout but then flipped to 100% at 12:08 to simplify analysis. That aligns with the spike. :grimacing:
maya: OK sounds like a config/regression from routing policy. We should stop the rollout and rollback traffic to the previous config immediately. @deploy-bot can you initiate rollback to routing-policy v1? :eyes: 
deploy-bot: Rollback requested by maya. Starting deployment: routing-policy v1 -> active. Canary completed (0/0 errors). Estimated rollback time ~90s.
sre-oncall: While rollback is running — need repro steps so support/sre can validate. Try this curl replicator against the gateway (use a small payload):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"lite-test","input":"short test"}' 
```
If you get 502/504 that's the same surface.

ashish: I'm seeing a config diff that looks suspicious — the rollout script changed `x-route-weight` semantics. Old policy sets `x-route-weight: 0.7` for small requests, new policy uses integer weights and some backends ended up with `0` weight. That can mark endpoints as unhealthy in our routing layer. Diff snippet:
```
- route_rules:
-  - match: size<1024
-    weight: 0.7
+ route_rules:
+  - match: size<1024
+    weight: 0
```
If weight==0 we occasionally short-circuit health checks depending on the router implementation — explains bursts of upstream resets.

kevin: Support has temporary workarounds: asking customers to retry and sending token refresh steps. I've created ticket #4389 and informed AE. support-bot created the ticket and sent initial message.
support-bot: Ticket #4389 created for customers impacted by routing-policy rollout. Notified customer owners and added status: investigating.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. routing-policy v1 active; traffic back to 100% v1 at 12:18 UTC. No further rollout tasks pending.

oliver: Verification — error rate dropped back to 0.25% within 2m after rollback. No more auth-service 500s. Metrics: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/xyz?range=15m :white_check_mark:

maya: Great. Post-incident next steps: 1) revert the feature flag gating for `route_v2_by_size` and block direct flips to 100% without canary enforcement; 2) add a preflight lint to detect zero-weight rules; 3) add an automated smoke test that fires the curl replicator after any routing config roll; 4) update runbook to include immediate rollback command and contact list.

emmie: Agreed — my bad for accelerating to 100%. I'll open the PR to add the lint and preflight. Also will add a post-rollout monitoring alert to hold on auto-promote.

ashish: I'll follow up with a short fix to make the router treat 0 weight as explicit exclude and not flip health-check behavior (defensive change).

kevin: Sent apology to affected customers, offered credits and provided ETA for RCA. CC'ed SRE and Product.

maya: Adding this to incidents backlog for a full blameless postmortem. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. :tada:

sre-oncall: Saving logs and traces to incident bucket: s3://incidents/1801456789/ and attaching to ticket #4389. If anyone has extra traces add them there.

support-bot: Follow-up: customers A and B acknowledged workaround and accepted temporary credits. Will update ticket when RCA is published.

oliver: Final check at 12:29 UTC — system stable, closing this thread unless new alerts appear.

maya: closing.
